Consistent with this, we observed no change to the steady state distribution of endogenously-expressed Chm7-GFP, which includes a minor fraction within a nuclear envelope focus in ~30% of cells (Webster et al., 2016; Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Deletion of the LEM domain of Heh1 had no effect on Chm7-GFP distribution as heh1(51-834)-RFP was also exclusively localized at the INM.
claims.source: Deletion of the LEM domain of Heh1 also had no effect on Chm7-GFP distribution as heh1(51-834)-RFP was also exclusively localized at the INM (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Expression of heh1(303-834) and heh1(442-834) resulted in the accumulation of these truncations throughout the cortical ER and a concurrent re-distribution of Chm7-GFP into foci that colocalized with the RFP signal.
claims.source: We next tested deletions that encompassed the putative NLSs in Heh1 including heh1(303-834), and heh1(442-834), which resulted in the accumulation of these truncations throughout the cortical ER. Strikingly, we observed a concurrent re-distribution of Chm7-GFP into foci that colocalized with the RFP signal (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: There was a complete lack of Chm7-GFP at the ER in cells expressing heh1(442-735), where the WH is removed.
claims.source: Consistent with this, there was a complete lack of Chm7-GFP at the ER in cells expressing heh1(442-735), where the WH is removed (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Exposure of the Heh1 WH domain to the cytosol is both necessary and sufficient to recruit Chm7-GFP to ER membranes.
claims.source: Thus, exposure of the Heh1 WH domain to the cytosol is both necessary and sufficient to recruit Chm7-GFP to ER membranes.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The loss of fitness observed in heh1Δapq12Δ cells could only be rescued by the gene encoding full length Heh1 or the heh1(51-834) allele.
claims.source: Interestingly, the loss of fitness observed in heh1Δapq12Δ cells could only be rescued by the gene encoding full length Heh1 or the heh1(51-834) allele.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Deletions that resulted in Heh1 mistargeting or those that are unable to recruit Chm7 were unable to fully complement growth in heh1Δapq12Δ cells.
claims.source: In contrast, deletions that resulted in Heh1 mistargeting or those that are unable to recruit Chm7 (e.g. heh1(1-735), which lacks the coding sequence for the WH domain) were unable to fully complement growth.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: While the WH domain is important, the N-terminal INM targeting domain is also a critical component of Heh1 functionality in the context of apq12Δ cells.
claims.source: Thus, while the WH domain is important, the N-terminal INM targeting domain is also a critical component of Heh1 functionality in the context of apq12Δ cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Few specific peptide spectra were detected with the exception of Chm7 itself when Chm7-GFP was affinity purified from whole cell extracts.
claims.source: Consistent with the idea that Chm7 is localized throughout the cytosol in a potentially inactive form, we detected few specific peptide spectra with the exception of Chm7 itself when compared to proteins derived from wildtype cell extracts that bind non-specifically to the anti-GFP beads (Figure 3A).

claims.claim: Affinity purification of Chm7-GFP from vps4Δpom152Δ cells revealed specific interactions with several ESCRTs including Snf7 and Vps36, and dozens of spectra specific for Heh1.
claims.source: Shot-gun MS identification of peptides derived from bound proteins to Chm7-GFP now revealed specific interactions with several ESCRTs including Snf7 and Vps36 (Figure 3B). Most interestingly, dozens of spectra specific for Heh1 were identified.
claims.evidence: This is supported by MS/MS data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Another low abundant integral INM protein, Nur1, was also detected in affinity purifications of Chm7-GFP from vps4Δpom152Δ cells.
claims.source: In addition, another low abundant (~354 molecules/cell; Kulak et al., 2014) integral INM protein, Nur1 was also detected.
claims.evidence: This is supported by MS/MS data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Chm7 engages Heh1 within a broader INM platform that includes Nur1.
claims.source: As Nur1 is known to interact with Heh1 within the CLIP (chromosome linkage INM proteins) complex (Mekhail et al., 2008), these data suggest that Chm7 engages Heh1 within a broader INM platform, at least in the context of cells lacking VPS4.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on MS/MS data and citation to prior work (Mekhail et al., 2008).

claims.claim: No components of the NPC were specifically detected in affinity purifications of Chm7-GFP from vps4Δpom152Δ cells, nor was Heh2.
claims.source: Of note, no components of the NPC were specifically detected, nor was Heh2.

claims.claim: Heh1 was the top hit in affinity purifications of chm7OPEN-GFP.

claims.claim: In addition to Nur1, other members of CLIP including Lrs4 and Csm1 were specifically identified in affinity purifications of chm7OPEN-GFP.
claims.source: In addition to Nur1, other members of CLIP were also specifically identified including Lrs4 and Csm1.
claims.evidence: This is supported by MS/MS data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Gsp1 (budding yeast Ran) was found in affinity purifications of chm7OPEN-GFP.
claims.source: Curiously, Gsp1 (budding yeast Ran) was also found (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by MS/MS data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Alongside Snf7, other ESCRT-IIIs including Vps2, Vps24 and Did2 were detected in affinity purifications of chm7OPEN-GFP.

results.result: Chm7 is actively exported from the nucleus by Xpo1/Crm1 via two conserved nuclear export signals (NESs) at its C-terminus. Inhibition of Xpo1 with Leptomycin B leads to nuclear accumulation of Chm7-GFP, while a large Chm7-MGM4 fusion that cannot passively diffuse through NPCs shows no LMB-dependent redistribution, indicating that Chm7 enters the nucleus by passive diffusion and is actively exported.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C4 and C50-C60 provide converging evidence from computational prediction (C51-C53), pharmacological inhibition (C54), size-exclusion experiments (C55), and functional NES reporter assays (C56-C58) that collectively demonstrate Xpo1-mediated nuclear export of Chm7. The data are internally consistent and the experimental controls (MGM4 fusion, NES reporters) are appropriate.

results.result: Calcium chelation with BAPTA-AM does not affect Chm7-GFP recruitment to the nuclear envelope in apq12Δ cells, suggesting that Ca2+ signaling is not a major contributor to Chm7 recruitment at the nuclear envelope.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C62 show that BAPTA-AM treatment had no effect on Chm7-GFP foci formation in apq12Δ cells (Figure 1H,I). While this is a negative result, the experimental approach is straightforward and the conclusion is appropriately cautious, stating Ca2+ is unlikely to be a 'major contributor' rather than claiming no role whatsoever.

results.result: The winged helix (WH) domain of Heh1 is necessary and sufficient to recruit Chm7 to membranes when exposed to the cytosol. Heh1 truncations lacking nuclear localization signals accumulate in the ER and recruit Chm7-GFP to these membranes, while removal of the WH domain abolishes this recruitment. Both the WH domain and proper INM targeting are required for Heh1 function in apq12Δ cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C71 present a systematic domain deletion analysis (Figure 2) showing that cytosolic exposure of the Heh1 WH domain is necessary and sufficient for Chm7 recruitment (C66-C68), while proper INM targeting requires the N-terminal domain (C69-C71). The genetic complementation data (C69-C70) support the functional importance of both domains. The experimental logic is sound and the conclusions are well-supported.

results.result: Chm7 interacts with Heh1, Nur1, and other CLIP complex components at the INM when recruited to the nuclear envelope. Mass spectrometry of Chm7-GFP from vps4Δpom152Δ cells and chm7OPEN-GFP identified Heh1 as a major interactor, along with Nur1, other CLIP components (Lrs4, Csm1), ESCRT-III proteins (Snf7, Vps2, Vps24, Did2), and Gsp1/Ran. Fluorescence microscopy confirmed near-quantitative recruitment of Heh1 and Nur1 to chm7OPEN foci.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C81 present complementary MS/MS (Figure 3A-C) and microscopy (Figure 3D) data demonstrating Chm7 interactions with an INM platform. The MS data show appropriate controls (no-GFP samples) and the specificity is validated by fluorescence colocalization. The detection of low-abundance INM proteins (Heh1, Nur1) in the MS data is particularly compelling given their reported cellular abundance (~400 molecules/cell).

results.result: Vps4 is recruited to chm7OPEN foci at the nuclear envelope in a manner dependent on Snf7 and downstream ESCRT-III components (Vps2, Vps24, Did2), but not on the endosomal ESCRT-III Vps20. Deletion of VPS20 actually increases Vps4-GFP recruitment ~3-fold, suggesting competition between endosomal and nuclear envelope ESCRT pathways for a limited Vps4 pool.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C86 demonstrate Vps4 recruitment requirements through systematic deletion analysis (Figure 3E). The correlation between Vps4-GFP and chm7OPEN-mCherry intensity (C83) supports a stoichiometric relationship. The striking increase in Vps4 recruitment upon VPS20 deletion (C85) provides strong evidence for pathway competition, though the interpretation (C86) is appropriately presented as inference. Western blots confirm equal Vps4 expression across strains.

results.result: Using the FETA (Fluorescence ESCRT Targeting and Activation) assay, Chm7-GFP recruitment to the INM via Heh2-GBP-mCherry is temporally separable from its activation. Chm7-GFP accumulates at the nuclear envelope within 20 minutes and forms clustered foci over 90 minutes in wildtype cells. In heh1Δ cells, Chm7-GFP still accumulates at the nuclear envelope but fails to form foci, demonstrating that Heh1 is required for Chm7 activation but not recruitment.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C93 describe a novel experimental system (FETA) that successfully decouples Chm7 recruitment from activation (Figure 4). The time-lapse data (C88, C91) and quantitative CV analysis (Figure 4C) provide robust evidence. The heh1Δ phenotype (C92-C93) is particularly informative, showing recruitment without activation. Appropriate controls confirm the GBP-dependence of the phenotype (C89).

results.result: Heh1's WH domain coupled to a membrane anchor is necessary and sufficient for Chm7 activation in the FETA assay. Nur1 contributes to activation, though this may be indirect through effects on Heh1 levels. Snf7 and Vps4 deletions do not prevent Heh2-GBP-mCherry clustering but alter the pattern of foci formation. The WH domain alone cannot rescue clustering in heh1Δ cells; membrane anchoring is required.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C103 use the FETA assay to dissect activation requirements (Figure 5). The domain analysis (C99-C103) clearly demonstrates that both the WH domain and membrane anchoring are required for activation. The Nur1 effect (C94-C96) is appropriately qualified as potentially indirect based on Western blot data showing reduced Heh1 levels. The Snf7/Vps4 results (C97-C98) suggest these factors affect downstream events not captured by the CV metric.

results.result: Correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM) reveals that sites of chm7OPEN-GFP accumulation correspond to fenestrated INM networks that invade the nucleus and nuclear envelope herniations extending into the cytosol. These herniations have ~45 nm diameter necks and are often associated with vesicles near the ONM. Similar structures form in the absence of Snf7 and in vps4Δpom152Δ cells with full-length Chm7-GFP.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C110 present striking CLEM data (Figures 6-7) showing membrane remodeling at Chm7 activation sites. The 3D tomographic reconstructions provide compelling visualization of the fenestrated INM networks and herniations. The quantification of neck diameter (C106) and frequency of associated features (C105, C107) strengthens the analysis. The observation that these structures form without Snf7 (C108) is important for mechanistic interpretation.

results.result: Nuclear envelope herniations in NPC assembly mutants (apq12Δ, nup116Δ) are morphologically distinct from those induced by Chm7 hyperactivation. NPC assembly-associated herniations have NPC components at their bases (confirmed by MAb414 immunogold labeling), wider necks (~78 nm vs ~45 nm), and electron-dense lumens, whereas Chm7-associated herniations have narrower necks and empty lumens.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C114 provide direct comparison between herniation types using immunogold EM (Figure 8A) and quantitative measurements (Figure 8B). The MAb414 labeling (C111) confirms NPC components at herniation bases in apq12Δ cells. The morphological differences in neck diameter (C112) and lumen contents (C113) are clearly documented. The conclusion of morphological distinction (C114) is well-supported by the comparative data.

results.result: While CHM7 deletion has minimal effect on herniation frequency in apq12Δ cells, 35% of apq12Δchm7Δ nuclei show large nuclear envelope ruptures (>500 nm discontinuities). Similar ruptures occur in apq12Δsnf7Δ cells. This indicates that while ESCRTs may not be required for herniation formation, they are essential for maintaining nuclear envelope integrity in the context of NPC assembly defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C115-C118 demonstrate a critical protective role for ESCRTs using thin-section EM (Figure 8B-E, supplements). The quantification shows modest reduction in herniations (C115) but dramatic increase in ruptures (C116) upon CHM7 deletion. The similar phenotype in snf7Δ (C117) supports ESCRT involvement. The conclusion (C118) appropriately distinguishes between herniation formation and membrane integrity maintenance.

results.result: Background on nuclear envelope organization and nuclear transport: NPCs impose a size-selective diffusion barrier (~40 kD cutoff) while facilitating active transport of signal-bearing cargo via nuclear transport receptors, with directionality provided by the Ran-GTPase gradient.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C8-C10 provide established background information supported by appropriate citations to prior work. These are well-accepted principles in the nuclear transport field and provide necessary context for the experimental work.

results.result: Background on nuclear envelope integrity and disease: Nuclear envelope barrier function is compromised in various diseases including neurodegenerative diseases (ALS, FTD), aging, and early-onset dystonia. Nuclear envelope herniations are associated with NPC assembly defects and may trigger ESCRT-dependent quality control pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C11-C19 summarize prior work on nuclear envelope dysfunction in disease contexts, all supported by appropriate citations. These establish the biological and medical relevance of the study. Some claims (C17, C18) appropriately note that certain mechanisms remain hypothetical.

results.result: Background on NPC assembly and quality control in yeast: Approximately 100 NPCs are assembled during the budding yeast cell cycle through INM evagination and membrane fusion. Malformed NPCs are not inherited by daughter cells, and ESCRT components (particularly Chm7) are required for viability in NPC assembly mutants. Heh2 has been proposed to surveil for malforming NPCs.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C25 provide relevant background on NPC assembly and quality control in yeast, supported by citations to prior work including the authors' own studies. Claim C25 appropriately notes that the surveillance signal remains to be formally established.

results.result: Background on ESCRT functions at the nuclear envelope in mammalian cells: ESCRTs function in nuclear envelope reformation at the end of mitosis, repair of nuclear ruptures during cell migration and mechanical stress, and potentially in NPC turnover in quiescent cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C29 summarize established roles for ESCRTs at the mammalian nuclear envelope, all supported by appropriate citations. These provide important comparative context for the yeast studies. Claim C28 appropriately qualifies the inference about mechanical stress-induced ruptures.

results.result: Background on Ca2+ in ESCRT recruitment: Ca2+ release triggers ESCRT recruitment at endolysosomes and the plasma membrane, potentially through the Ca2+-binding protein ALG-2.
results.evaluation: Claim C30 provides relevant background on Ca2+ signaling in other ESCRT pathways, supported by appropriate citations. This contextualizes the negative result regarding Ca2+ in the nuclear envelope pathway (C61-C62).

results.result: Background on ESCRT-III assembly and function: ESCRT-III polymers (primarily Snf7/CHMP4B) scaffold membrane curvature and contribute to membrane scission. Vps4 disassembles ESCRT-III filaments by threading them through its hexameric ring, likely contributing force for scission. Different ESCRT recruitment mechanisms operate at endosomes versus the nuclear envelope, with Vps25 and Vps20 absent from the nuclear envelope pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C37 provide essential background on ESCRT-III mechanisms, all supported by appropriate citations to prior structural and biochemical work. The distinction between endosomal and nuclear envelope pathways (C36-C37) is important for interpreting the current results.

results.result: Background on Chm7-Heh1 interactions: Chm7, Heh1, and Heh2 interact biochemically and genetically with Snf7. Heh1 is required for Chm7 focal accumulation in NPC assembly mutants. The Heh1-Chm7 interaction is conserved in fission yeast and mammals (LEM2-CHMP7).
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C41 summarize prior work on Chm7-Heh1 interactions from the authors' previous studies and others, providing direct context for the current mechanistic investigations. The evolutionary conservation (C40-C41) supports the biological significance.

results.result: Background on LEM domain protein structure and function: Heh1 and Heh2 contain an N-terminal LEM domain, an INM targeting sequence with NLS and unstructured region, and a C-terminal winged helix (WH) domain. LEM proteins interface with chromatin, contribute to rDNA stability and nuclear mechanical robustness, and their loss leads to nuclear envelope disruption in diverse yeast species.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C49 provide comprehensive background on LEM protein structure and function, all supported by appropriate citations. This information is essential for interpreting the domain deletion experiments and understanding the dual roles of Heh1 in nuclear integrity and ESCRT recruitment.
